content: ALCAM, also known as CD166 antigen, is a transmembrane glycoprotein with a molecular weight of approximately 100-105 kDa. It belongs to the immunoglobulin superfamily of proteins. In humans, the ALCAM gene encodes this protein. It is also referred to as CD166 (Cluster of Differentiation 166), MEMD, SC-1/DM-GRASP/BEN in chickens, and KG-CAM in rats. Some studies have also identified it as the CD6 ligand (CD6L). This protein is expressed on various cell types, including activated T cells, activated monocytes, epithelial cells, fibroblasts, neurons, melanoma cells, and in sweat and sebaceous glands. Notably, the expression of CD166 is reported to be upregulated in cell lines derived from metastatic melanoma, suggesting its involvement in cancer progression. CD166 plays a critical role in mediating adhesion interactions between thymic epithelial cells and CD6+ cells during the development of T cells within the thymus. Furthermore, recent research has highlighted its potential as a marker for cancer stem cells, indicating its importance in oncology and cancer biology.
